source_text:
Εἰ πρὸς τὴν ἀδόλεσχον καὶ πολυεπῆ Μαρκέλλου γραφὴν τὰ παρ’ ἡμῶν ἐν βραχέσιν ἤρκεσεν, οὐ χρὴ θαυμάζειν· οὐ γὰρ δὴ πολλῶν ἔδει λόγων πρὸς ἀνατροπὴν τῶν αὐτόθεν καὶ τοῖς τυχοῦσιν κατεγνωσμένων. διὸ δὴ ἐν δυσὶ τοῖς πρώτοις μόνῃ τῇ παραθέσει τῶν τοῦ ἀνδρὸς ῥημάτων χρησάμενος δίχα πάσης ἀντιρρήσεως ἐξ αὐτῶν τὸν κατ’ αὐτῶν ἔλεγχον φανερὸν ἐποιούμην. νυνὶ δὲ πρὸς ἐκείνῃ τῇ φώρᾳ καὶ τὴν ἀνατροπὴν τῶν αὐτῶν διὰ τριῶν τῶν μετὰ χεῖρας προσήγαγον. ὁ μὲν γὰρ ἕν τι διωλύγιον καὶ πολυπλανὲς σύγγραμμα συντάξας τοῦτό φησιν πεποιηκέναι διὰ τὸ ἕνα γνωρίζειν θεόν, μή πη λάθῃ τῷ υἱῷ τοῦ θεοῦ χώραν διδοὺς ὑποστάσεως διελὼν τὴν γραφήν. ἡμεῖς δὲ τὴν παναγίαν καὶ τρισμακαρίαν τιμῶντες τριάδα ἐν τοσούτοις τὴν πᾶσαν ὑπόθεσιν συνειλήφαμεν, φεισάμενοι μὲν πολυλογίας, ἐν ἐπιτόμοις δὲ καὶ βραχέσιν τὴν ἀληθῆ παραστήσαντες θεολογίαν. εἰ μὲν οὖν αὐταρκῶς ἔχει τὰ γραφέντα, κρίνειας ἂν αὐτὸς ἐντυγχάνων· εἰ δέ τινα λείποι, καὶ ταῦτα 〈ἂν〉 ἀναπληρώσειας, δηλαδὴ [ἃ δὴ] ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφοῦ τὰ ὑστερήματα, εἴ που καὶ θεραπείας δέοιτο, δι’ ἐπανορθώσεως ἐξιώμενος.
Ἔρρωσθαί σε καὶ μνημονεύειν μου τῷ κυρίῳ διὰ παντὸς εὔχομαι.
orientation: Eusebius opens his letter to Flacillus by explaining why his short reply to Marcellus' wordy treatise was enough.
pass_a_gloss: If against the babbling and wordy treatise of Marcellus the things from us in brief sufficed, it is not necessary to wonder; for indeed there was no need of many words for the refutation of the things condemned on the spot and even by ordinary people. Therefore indeed in the first two books using only the quotation of the man's words apart from every counter-argument from them the exposure against them I was making evident. But now in addition to that exposure also the refutation of the same things through the three books at hand I have brought forward. For he, having composed one enormous and much-wandering treatise, says he has done this because he knows one God, dividing the treatise so that he might not somehow escape notice giving the Son of God room for a distinct person. But we, honoring the all-holy and thrice-blessed Trinity, in so many words have comprehended the whole subject, sparing indeed wordiness, and in concise and brief terms having presented the true theology. If then sufficiently the things written hold, you yourself would judge as you read; but if any things are lacking, these too you would fill up, clearly as a brother the shortcomings of a brother, if somewhere also of healing it should need, making up for it through correction. I pray that you be strong and remember me to the Lord always.

choices.why: Captures the pejorative sense of idle, excessive talk aimed at Marcellus' treatise.
Plain and direct; matches the contrast with Eusebius' brevity.
Idiomatic rendering of 'those who happen to be there', meaning anyone at all.
Conveys the size and excess of Marcellus' single treatise.
Literal rendering preserving the compound's force of wandering in many directions.
The verb means to supply or make good what is lacking, not to require; agency is with the brother who fills the gap.

pass_b_english: If our brief response sufficed against Marcellus' babbling, wordy treatise, there is no need to wonder. For no lengthy arguments were needed to refute things condemned on the spot even by ordinary people. Therefore, in the first two books I used only the quotation of the man's words, without any counter-argument, and made the exposure against them evident from the words themselves. Now, in addition to that exposure, I have also brought forward the refutation of the same points through the three books at hand. For he composed one enormous, much-wandering treatise and says he did this because he makes one God known, dividing the treatise so that it might not somehow escape him to give the Son of God room for a distinct person. But we, honoring the all-holy and thrice-blessed Trinity, have gathered the whole subject into these few books, sparing lengthy speech and presenting the true theology concisely and briefly. If, then, what has been written is sufficient, you yourself may judge as you read. But if anything is lacking, you may fill these gaps too—clearly, as a brother would supply a brother's deficiencies—making up for it through correction wherever healing may be needed. I pray that you fare well and remember me before the Lord always.

problems.why: γνωρίζειν means 'make known' not 'know'; Marcellus claims to proclaim one God, not merely know him.
problems.fix: because he makes one God known

problems.quote: he might not somehow be caught
problems.why: λάθῃ is subjunctive of λανθάνω with dative: 'so that it might escape his notice,' not passive 'be caught.' Marcellus actively avoids, not caught.
problems.fix: lest it somehow escape him to give the Son of God room for a distinct person
problems.ruling: μή πη λάθῃ = 'lest it escape his notice'; 'be caught' reverses meaning from oversight to detection

edits.old: he might not somehow be caught giving the Son of God room for a distinct person
edits.new: it might not somehow escape him to give the Son of God room for a distinct person

fixed: Changed 'he knows one God' to 'he makes one God known' because γνωρίζειν means 'make known,' not 'know.'

Changed 'he might not somehow be caught giving the Son of God room for a distinct person' to 'it might not somehow escape him to give the Son of God room for a distinct person' because λάθῃ is active with dative, meaning 'escape his notice,' not passive 'be caught.'

last_rejected.why: Infinitive 'γνωρίζειν' is purpose, not habitual; 'makes known' implies ongoing action, not intent.
last_rejected.fix: because he wished to make one God known
last_rejected.ruling: 'makes known' correctly renders γνωρίζειν; context already has 'because' (διὰ τό) showing purpose. No meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: it might not somehow escape him
last_rejected.why: Subject of λάθῃ is the danger, not 'it'; 'escape him' misrepresents the Greek construction.
last_rejected.fix: lest he somehow inadvertently give the Son of God room for a distinct person
last_rejected.ruling: μή πη λάθῃ + dative αὐτῷ = 'lest it escape him'; standard Greek idiom correctly rendered. No misrepresentation.

last_rejected.why: Participial phrase explains how he composed it, not purpose; 'so that' makes it result/purpose clause.
last_rejected.ruling: διελὼν τὴν γραφήν as participial phrase alongside φησιν πεποιηκέναι; 'dividing...so that' reads naturally. No real error.

last_rejected.quote: gathered the whole subject into these few books
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐν τοσούτοις τὴν πᾶσαν ὑπόθεσιν συνειλήφαμεν
last_rejected.why: ἐν τοσούτοις means 'in so brief a compass,' not 'into these few books' which adds specificity.
last_rejected.fix: have compressed the whole subject into so brief a compass
last_rejected.ruling: ἐν τοσούτοις = 'in so many/brief books'; 'into these few books' is reasonable contextual rendering. No meaning change or added specificity.
